themes_detail.label: Public Drinking Surge
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints exploded to 10 this week—a 3900% spike versus 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 14.74)—suggesting a sudden enforcement crackdown, organized activity, or new venue in Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights that warrants immediate reporting.
evidence: 10 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3900% increase)
Z-score of 14.74 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
No pattern visible in prior data—suggests sudden emergence or enforcement change
reporting_angles: Investigate whether NYPD launched new enforcement operation on public drinking in the district this week
Identify which blocks or venues are driving the complaints—interview 311 callers and local precinct about hotspots

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints jumped 71% last week to 190 versus 110.9 weekly average (z-score: 6.73), indicating a sustained uptick in apartment/building noise that may reflect construction, new tenant populations, or venue activity.
evidence: 190 residential noise complaints last week vs. 110.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (71% increase)
Residential noise is already the #2 complaint type overall (1586 over 90 days), now accelerating
reporting_angles: Map complaints by block to identify noise hotspots—is it concentrated around one building, venue, or construction site?
Speak with residents in high-complaint areas about what changed—new bar, late-night venue, construction start date?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked 700% two weeks ago to 17 versus 2.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.62), suggesting either aggressive street vending activity or city enforcement crackdowns targeting street vendors in the district.
evidence: 17 vendor enforcement complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase)
Z-score of 4.62 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Timing suggests either new vendor operations or city enforcement initiative launched around that date
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD/DOC enforcement—did they launch a street vending operation in this district two weeks ago?
Interview street vendors and local businesses about enforcement intensity and impact on commerce

themes_detail.label: Tree/Vegetation Emergencies
themes_detail.summary: Plant-related complaints (1100% spike, 3 this week vs. 0.2 avg) and overgrown tree/branch complaints (357% spike, 4 last week vs. 0.9 avg) suggest rapid vegetation overgrowth or storm damage—possibly related to recent rain or delayed Parks maintenance.
evidence: 3 plant complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score: 4.16)
4 overgrown tree/branch complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (357% increase, z-score: 4.0)
Community board budget requests consistently cite need for vegetation management—indicating chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Check weather data—was there heavy rain or wind this past week that triggered tree damage or overgrowth complaints?
Contact Parks Dept about maintenance backlog and response times for tree/vegetation complaints in CD109

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints spiked 500% three weeks ago (3 complaints vs. 0.5 avg, z-score: 5.0), pointing to potential tap water contamination, discoloration, or taste/odor complaints that may affect multiple buildings.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 5.0)
No ongoing pattern—spike was isolated but statistically significant
Heat/hot water is the #1 complaint type (2305 over 90 days), suggesting infrastructure vulnerabilities
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to investigate what triggered water quality complaints 3 weeks ago—was there a main break, treatment issue, or boil water advisory?
Identify which buildings filed complaints and interview residents about water discoloration, taste, or odor issues
